summary: Trace timeline missing for some requests; alert notifications delayed after retention TTL change
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report that request-level traces are intermittently absent from the Console request timeline for a subset of calls originating from HelixHealth's production workspace. At the same time, alert notifications tied to error-rate thresholds are arriving 8–12 minutes after the incident onset. Both symptoms started after HelixHealth updated their retention TTL for trace events from 30d to 7d via the Console UI on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- HelixHealth (enterprise) cannot correlate failed inference requests with trace spans for debugging.
- Delayed alerting increases mean time to detect for SLA-impacting errors.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (hosted) - prod region us-east.
- Affected workspace: helixhealth-prod (customer attached account).
- Model: gpt-redwood-14b-v2 pinned on latest-serving revision.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) In HelixHealth prod, issue inference calls that occasionally return 5xx or streaming disconnects.
2) Open Console > Requests > select a request ID seen by the customer.
3) Expect to see trace timeline with span breakdown; sometimes timeline is empty or shows only top-level request event.
4) Trigger an error spike (simulated by replay) and observe alert delivery time in Slack webhook and email. Notifications are delivered 8–12 minutes after the spike begins.

Observed behavior:
- ~30% of failed requests in a sampled period show no tracing spans in the UI.
- Alerting pipeline shows processing lag; queue depth increases at the time of spikes.

Expected behavior:
- All instrumented requests should surface spans and the full timeline in Console within seconds.
- Alerts should evaluate and deliver within configured evaluation window (default 1 minute) and notify stakeholders promptly.

Attachments/logs:
- Customer provided two request IDs and timestamps (attached in ticket).
- Support grabs from request logs and alerting metrics: link to support S3 bundle attached.

Note: Customer changed trace-retention TTL immediately prior to the incident; they believe the UI change may have triggered a backend compaction / reindex operation.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Maya Chen (Reporter): Filing on behalf of HelixHealth. They performed a TTL change for trace retention via Console on 2026-03-09 23:40 UTC. Since then they've seen missing spans and slower alert notifications. Provided sample request IDs: RH-20260309-9981, RH-20260310-1042.

2026-03-10 10:27 - Raj Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Opening investigation. Assigning to tracing/alerts owners and SRE. First check: verify retention change events and any background compaction jobs around that time. Asking HelixHealth for exact workspace ID and whether they observed increased 5xx rates at the TTL change time.

2026-03-10 11:05 - SRE (Anya Sokolov): Observed a background retention compaction job kick at 2026-03-09T23:42Z for tenant helixhealth-prod. Compaction ran across several storage shards in us-east; some shards reported transient resource contention (IO wait). Collecting alert pipeline metrics and queue lengths now.

2026-03-10 12:40 - Eng (Leo Martinez - tracing): Reproduced missing spans in a synthetic load against a canary workspace when we simulate retention TTL change followed by compaction. Hypothesis: index compaction temporarily disables span-extraction worker for affected shards leading to a short window where spans are persisted but not indexed to the query store, so Console queries return incomplete timelines. Working on a fix to make compaction non-blocking for indexing.

2026-03-10 14:20 - SRE (Anya Sokolov): Alerting pipeline backlog correlated with a downstream Kafka consumer rebalancing when compaction increased partition lag. Consumer lag peaked at ~1.2M messages and processing latency jumped causing evaluation delays. We're throttling compaction on remaining tenants as mitigation.

2026-03-11 09:02 - Raj Patel (Support): Shared mitigation steps with customer: we paused further retention updates, temporarily increased alert evaluation concurrency for helixhealth-prod, and scheduled a reindex window. Customer accepted the workaround and asked for ETA on permanent fix.

2026-03-12 15:45 - Leo Martinez (Eng): Deployed a hotfix to the compaction process to allow asynchronous span index updates and reduce impact on Kafka consumer groups. Patch rolled to us-east staging then to prod with canary. Monitoring for reappearance of missing spans and reduced alert lag.

2026-03-12 16:02 - HelixHealth (Customer comment via email): Reported that earlier missing traces are now populating after reindex and new alerts triggered within expected windows. Asking for postmortem and suggestions to avoid future disruption when changing retention settings.
investigation_notes: Initial correlation: TTL change triggered compaction job starting 2026-03-09T23:42Z on helixhealth-prod tenant.
Storage observation: compaction caused increased disk IO on several trace store shards (s-us-east-04, s-us-east-05). IO wait increased to 85% for 12 minutes.

Indexing behavior: compaction path originally paused span-indexer worker to avoid conflicting writes; this created a short period where spans were accepted but not indexed into the query search store.

Alert pipeline: Kafka consumer group 'alerts-evaluator-us-east' experienced rebalances tied to retention job causing message-processing latency to increase; evaluation windows missed and notifications delayed by ~8-12m.

Reproduction: Created canary workspace, changed TTL from 30d -> 7d and observed same sequence: compaction -> indexing pause -> missing spans in Console queries -> alert evaluation lag. Reproducible on staging with synthetic traffic.

Risk assessment: Non-zero risk for other enterprise tenants that perform bulk retention TTL updates during peak traffic windows. Impact limited to trace visibility and alert timeliness, not to core inference serving (tokens still processed).
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-10: Paused retention compaction for remaining scheduled jobs for 3 hours; increased alerting consumer concurrency for helixhealth-prod to drain backlog.

Hotfix rolled 2026-03-12: compaction changed to asynchronous index-updates to avoid pausing span-indexer. Deployed to us-east with canary and monitored for 48h. Commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/commit/2f9b7c3f.
Reindex performed for helixhealth-prod to backfill missing span indexes; previously missing timelines now available. Provided reindex report to customer (attached).
Follow-ups assigned: INT-411 to add throttling for tenant-wide heavy retention ops; INT-412 to add runbook steps and a Console warning modal for retention changes during high-traffic windows.

Customer communication: Sent summary email and scheduled a 1:1 postmortem with HelixHealth for 2026-03-16. Customer confirmed improved behavior and requested clear UI guidance before changing retention TTLs.

Status: Monitoring — no new recurrences observed in us-east as of 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC. Marking customer ticket resolved when HelixHealth acknowledges PM and runbook items; support will keep ticket open until postmortem meeting completes.
